title: Dissociative amnesia: inability to recall a traumatic event
vignette: A 17-year-old girl is brought to the office by her parents for evaluation following the accidental drowning of her younger sister a week ago. The patient, her sister, and 2 friends had gone swimming in the ocean. When the sister became submerged, the patient attempted to rescue her but was overpowered by strong rip currents and was forced to return to shore. The mother is concerned that her daughter seems to be unaware of her sister's death and believes she is "in denial." The patient was unable to answer questions from the police about the drowning and reports she cannot remember any details of what happened that day. Physical examination is unremarkable. On mental status examination, the patient is alert and fully oriented. She becomes upset and confused when the incident is discussed. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

clues.text: accidental drowning of her younger sister a week ago
clues.note: An overwhelming, life-threatening traumatic event is the typical precipitant of dissociative amnesia. (Sensitive topic - addressed as clinical care.)

clues.text: cannot remember any details of what happened that day
clues.note: A selective inability to recall important autobiographical information about a specific traumatic event - beyond ordinary forgetfulness - defines dissociative amnesia.
Being alert and fully oriented (intact consciousness/cognition) argues against a neurologic or substance-induced amnesia.

whatMatters: An isolated, selective inability to recall a specific OVERWHELMING traumatic event (the sister's drowning), in an otherwise alert and oriented patient, is DISSOCIATIVE AMNESIA. The memory gap is beyond ordinary forgetfulness and typically follows trauma. Answer D.
strategy: Match to dissociative amnesia: localized/selective amnesia for a traumatic event, sudden onset, no neurologic/substance cause, patient otherwise intact. Reject PTSD (requires hyperarousal, intrusive memories/flashbacks, avoidance, >1 month), adjustment disorder (emotional/behavioral symptoms to a non-life-threatening stressor), complicated grief (persistent >6-12 months, yearning), and conversion disorder (motor/sensory neurologic symptoms).

eliminations.label: Adjustment disorder - non-life-threatening stressor
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: emotional/behavioral symptoms in response to an identifiable, non-life-threatening psychosocial stressor. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it doesn't explain a selective AMNESIA for an overwhelming traumatic event. ✅ Correct if: distress out of proportion to a milder stressor (job loss, breakup).

eliminations.label: Complicated grief reaction - persistent yearning, not amnesia
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a prolonged (>=6-12 months) grief with intense yearning, rumination, and dysfunction. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is a persistent grief disorder, not a sudden amnesia one week after the loss. ✅ Correct if: disabling grief lasting many months.

eliminations.label: Conversion disorder - motor/sensory neurologic symptoms
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: functional neurologic symptoms (weakness, sensory loss, nonepileptic seizures) incompatible with disease. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this patient has memory loss, not the motor/sensory deficits required for conversion disorder. ✅ Correct if: functional limb weakness/sensory loss after stress.

eliminations.label: PTSD - needs hyperarousal/intrusion/avoidance >1 month (your pick)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: posttraumatic stress disorder - trauma plus intrusive memories/nightmares, hyperarousal, avoidance, lasting >1 month. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: although amnesia for the trauma can occur in PTSD, this patient (1 week out) lacks the other required symptoms, and the isolated amnesia best fits dissociative amnesia. ✅ Correct if: full PTSD symptom cluster present for >1 month.

reasoning: Overwhelming trauma (sister's drowning) followed by a selective inability to recall that day's events
Patient is otherwise alert and fully oriented (no neurologic/substance cause)
Selective/localized amnesia for a traumatic event beyond ordinary forgetfulness = dissociative amnesia
mechanism: Dissociative amnesia is an inability to recall important autobiographical information - usually of a traumatic or stressful nature - that is too extensive to be explained by ordinary forgetfulness. The amnesia is most often LOCALIZED or SELECTIVE for a particular event (as here, the sister's drowning), though it can be generalized (loss of identity/personal history); onset is typically sudden and follows an overwhelming, intolerable experience. Diagnosis requires ruling out substances (e.g., alcohol blackout) and neurologic conditions (e.g., head trauma), and the patient is otherwise cognitively intact (alert, fully oriented). It reflects a dissociative defense that keeps distressing memories out of conscious awareness. Amnesia for a traumatic event can also occur as one feature of acute/posttraumatic stress disorder, but PTSD additionally requires intrusive re-experiencing (nightmares/flashbacks), hyperarousal, and avoidance persisting >1 month - which this patient (one week out, with isolated amnesia) does not meet. Treatment is supportive psychotherapy in a safe environment; memories often return over time. (Sensitive topic: grief and trauma support are appropriate; I can help find resources.)

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Psych > dissociative amnesia: localized/selective inability to recall traumatic autobiographical info; sudden onset after trauma; rule out substances/neurologic causes; distinct from PTSD (needs full symptom cluster >1 month).

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Isolated amnesia for a specific trauma, patient otherwise intact = dissociative amnesia (not full PTSD).

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on dissociative amnesia, localized/selective vs generalized amnesia, PTSD criteria, or conversion disorder? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: PTSD needs intrusion/hyperarousal/avoidance >1 month; adjustment disorder = milder stressor; complicated grief = persistent; conversion = motor/sensory.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: dissociative amnesia = trauma-related selective memory loss, intact orientation, no organic cause; supportive therapy. Sensitive topic - resources available.

keywords.front: Selective inability to recall a traumatic event, otherwise intact
Must rule out before diagnosing dissociative amnesia

keywords.back: Intrusion, hyperarousal, avoidance, negative mood; >1 month
Motor/sensory neurologic deficits incompatible with disease

firstAid.detail: Psych: trauma-related selective memory loss; intact orientation; rule out organic causes.
Psych > PTSD (full cluster >1 mo), adjustment disorder, complicated grief, conversion.
Psych > supportive psychotherapy; memories often return.

memoryHook: The mind walls off an unbearable day: she's alert and oriented but simply cannot retrieve her sister's drowning - selective dissociative amnesia, not the full PTSD picture.
